A.q: A hydraulic system has a small piston of area 0.02 m² and a large piston of area 0.8 m². If 150 N is applied on the small piston, what is the output force on the large piston?
The strength of a material refers to its ability to:
A.explain: Strength = ability to withstand applied stress without failure.

A.q: A fully submerged object has volume 0.050 m³ in fresh water (ρ=1000 kg/m³, g=9.8). Buoyant force?
The force exerted by a fluid on a submerged object is always:
options: Perpendicular to the object's surface, and increases with depth
A.explain: Fluid force on a surface is perpendicular (normal) to it and increases with depth.

A.q: A strain value is best characterised as:
A.explain: Strain = ΔL / L₀ — a ratio of two lengths, so units cancel. It is dimensionless.

A.q: How many nanometres (nm) are in 1 micrometre (µm)?
A.explain: 1 µm = 10⁻⁶ m and 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m, so 1 µm = 10³ nm = 1000 nm.

A.q: The equation of continuity in its general form is:
options: P₁ + ½ ρ v₁² = P₂ + ½ ρ v₂²
ρ₁ A₁ v₁ = ρ₂ A₂ v₂
A.explain: As long as no fluid is being added or taken out, the flow rate between any two points must be equal: ρ₁ A₁ v₁ = ρ₂ A₂ v₂.

A.q: Convert a systolic pressure of 150 mmHg to pascals. (1 mmHg ≈ 133.3 Pa)
In laminar flow, where is the velocity of the blood highest?
options: In the centre of the vessel
It is uniform across the vessel
A.explain: Velocity is highest in the centre of the vessel and lowest near the vessel wall. The profile is parabolic.

A.q: In a static fluid, how does pressure behave at a given depth?
options: It acts equally in all directions
A.explain: At a given depth in a static fluid, pressure acts equally in all directions.

A.q: A bone that bends slightly under load and returns to its original shape when the load is removed is displaying:
A.explain: Elasticity = returns to original shape after force removal. This is normal bone behaviour under physiological loads.

A.q: The modulus of elasticity reflects which property of a material?
options: Its stiffness or resistance to deformation
A.explain: Modulus = Stress / Strain. High modulus means a lot of stress is needed to produce a small strain — that is stiffness.

A.q: Blood (ρ ≈ 1050 kg/m³) flows through a vessel of area 2.0×10⁻⁴ m² at 0.40 m/s. Mass flow rate ṁ?
Cortical bone specimen: L = 0.20 m, A = 1.0×10⁻⁴ m², F = 1000 N, ΔL = 0.12 mm. Calculate the Young's modulus.
options: Both A and B are the same number
A.explain: Stress = 1000 / 1×10⁻⁴ = 1.0×10⁷ Pa. Strain = 1.2×10⁻⁴ / 0.20 = 6.0×10⁻⁴. Young's modulus = 1.0×10⁷ / 6.0×10⁻⁴ = 1.67×10¹⁰ Pa = 16.7×10⁹ Pa. A and B describe the same value.

A.q: Bernoulli's Principle states that for a steady, incompressible, negligible-viscosity, streamline flow, the total energy per unit volume — consisting of which three components — is constant throughout the flow?
options: Pressure, potential energy, and kinetic energy
A.explain: The total energy per unit volume — pressure plus potential energy plus kinetic energy — is constant throughout a streamline flow.

A.q: Longitudinal stress is applied:
options: Along the axis (length) of the object
A.explain: Longitudinal stress acts along the length of the material, either as tensile (stretching) or compressive (squeezing).

A.q: In Torricelli’s mercury barometer, a column height of about 76 cm of Hg corresponds to:
A.explain: Standard atmospheric pressure supports ~76 cm (760 mm) of mercury ≈ 1.013×10⁵ Pa.

A.q: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a condition in which:
options: Bones have unusually high Young's modulus
Bones are brittle with lower Young's modulus and easily fractured
A.explain: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a genetic condition producing brittle bones with lower Young's modulus and high fracture risk.

A.q: Which best explains why our cells are not crushed by atmospheric pressure?
options: The body is shielded by a vacuum
Cells maintain an internal pressure that balances atmospheric pressure
A.explain: Internal pressure balances external atmospheric pressure.

A.q: Density ρ equals mass m divided by volume V. With m in grams and V in cm³, ρ is in:
A.explain: Matching units: grams over cubic centimetres give g·cm⁻³. Water is about 1.00 g·cm⁻³. 1 g·cm⁻³ = 1000 kg·m⁻³.

B.q: How many types of modulus of elasticity exist, and what are they?
options: Three: Young's modulus, Shear modulus, Bulk modulus
B.explain: Three types, each matched to a specific geometry of stress and strain: Young's modulus (longitudinal), Shear modulus (tangential), Bulk modulus (volume).

B.q: The buoyant force on a submerged object arises because:
options: Pressures at the top and bottom of the object are different
Gravity acts only on the object
B.explain: Pressure increases with depth, so the bottom face feels a larger upward force than the top face.

B.q: Which of the following is an ADDITIONAL state of matter beyond solid, liquid, and gas?
B.explain: Plasma and Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC) are the additional states mentioned in the lecture.

B.q: In Pascal's principle, if the area of the small piston is halved while the applied force stays the same, what happens to the pressure in the hydraulic fluid?
B.explain: P = F/A. Same F, half A → pressure doubles.

B.q: Diagram (b) shows a cylinder whose top face slides sideways by Δx. This represents:
B.explain: Force parallel to the surface causing sliding is shear stress. The cylinder deforms like a pack of playing cards pushed sideways.

B.q: Pressure is defined as:
B.explain: P = F/A. SI unit: pascal (Pa) = N/m².

B.q: What is the specific gravity of a substance?
options: Its mass divided by its volume
Its volume divided by its mass
The ratio of its density to the density of water
B.explain: Specific gravity = ρ_substance / ρ_water (dimensionless).

B.q: In turbulent blood flow, how do the layers move?
options: Both radially and axially — the layers mix
They do not move at all
B.explain: In turbulent flow, blood layers mix and run radially and axially — sideways and along the vessel.

B.q: What is the correct relationship between stress and strain within the elastic limit?
options: Stress and strain are inversely proportional
Stress is always numerically equal to strain
Stress and strain are directly proportional
B.explain: Within the elastic limit, stress ∝ strain — the slope of that line is the Young's modulus.

B.q: Compressive stress applied to a material causes it to:
B.explain: Compressive stress pushes the ends together, shortening the material. It is a form of longitudinal stress.

B.q: An artery has cross-section A₁ = 4.0×10⁻⁴ m² with blood speed 0.25 m/s. After a narrowing to A₂ = 1.0×10⁻⁴ m², what is the new speed (incompressible)?
Which of the following is NOT one of the four unit systems named in the lecture?
B.explain: The lecture names CGS, FPS, MKS, and SI. GPS is a positioning system, not a unit system.

B.q: What is the difference between mass flow rate and volume flow rate?
options: They are exactly the same quantity
Mass flow rate is only used for gases, volume flow rate only for liquids
Mass flow rate tracks volume per unit time; volume flow rate tracks mass per unit time
Mass flow rate tracks mass per unit time (ρAv); volume flow rate tracks volume per unit time (Av)
B.explain: Mass flow rate = ρAv, with SI unit kg/s. Volume flow rate = Av, with SI unit m³/s.

B.q: A vessel narrows from A₁ = 0.08 m² (v₁ = 0.4 m/s) to A₂ = 0.02 m². For incompressible flow, v₂?
In these Medical Physics lectures, the symbol ρ (rho) stands for:
B.explain: ρ = density (m/V). P = pressure. σ = stress. ε = strain.

B.q: Malleability is the property of being:
B.explain: Malleable = can be hammered/rolled into sheets. Ductile = can be drawn into wires.

B.q: The density (ρ) of an object is defined as:
B.explain: ρ = m/V. SI unit kg/m³ (also g/cm³ on the bench).

B.q: Shear strain is calculated as:
B.explain: Shear strain = Δx / L, where Δx is the horizontal displacement of one face and L is the perpendicular height.

B.q: Which law states that if an external pressure is applied to a confined fluid, the pressure at every point increases by the same amount?
B.explain: That is Pascal's Law (P_in = P_out).

B.q: Hydraulic lift: A_small = 0.01 m², A_large = 0.10 m². Input force to lift 1500 N?

C.q: Systolic arterial pressure 145 mm Hg in kPa approximately? (1 mmHg ≈ 133.3 Pa)
Pascal’s principle states that an external pressure applied to a confined fluid:
options: Increases the pressure by that amount at every point in the fluid
Acts only at the free surface
C.explain: In a confined fluid, applied pressure is transmitted undiminished to every point (basis of hydraulics).

C.q: The lecture diagram (a) shows a cylinder being stretched lengthwise by ΔL. This represents:
C.explain: Force along the axis pulling the ends apart = tensile longitudinal stress. Result: elongation ΔL.

C.q: Buoyant force on a box of volume 0.24 m³ fully submerged in fresh water (ρ=1000 kg/m³, g=9.8)?
How much does the gauge pressure increase for every 10 m of depth in fresh water? (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²)
Bernoulli's equation can be written compactly as:
C.explain: P + ½ρv² + ρgh = const along a streamline.

C.q: Gauge pressure at depth 12 m in fresh water (ρ=1000 kg/m³, g=9.8)?
Blood flow through a narrowed artery is expected to be:
C.explain: Blood flow through a narrowed artery becomes turbulent. Heart valve disease may also produce turbulence and heart murmurs.

C.q: Blood in the human body is best classified, in this lecture's terms, as which state of matter?
C.explain: Blood behaves as a liquid: no definite shape, nearly fixed volume, moderate intermolecular forces, not easily compressible.

C.q: What is the difference between ductility and malleability?
options: Ductility = hammered into sheets; Malleability = drawn into thin wires
Ductility = drawn into thin wires; Malleability = hammered or rolled into sheets
C.explain: Ductile = can be drawn into wires. Malleable = can be hammered into sheets.

C.q: Blood flows at 0.3 m/s where area is 2.0×10⁻⁴ m². Stenosis to 0.5×10⁻⁴ m². New speed (incompressible)?
Hydraulic (volume) stress is:
options: Force applied at a single point
Uniform pressure applied from all sides by a fluid
Force applied tangentially to the surface
C.explain: Hydraulic stress is uniform pressure distributed equally from all directions — like an object submerged in fluid.

C.q: A hydraulic press has a small piston of area 0.015 m² and a large piston of area 1.2 m². What output force results from an input force of 200 N?
Which of the following is a consequence of turbulent blood flow?
options: Reduced tissue perfusion and possible murmur
C.explain: Turbulent flow can result in reduced tissue perfusion, and vessels may produce a murmur.

C.q: A cortical bone specimen is 0.15 m long with cross-sectional area 0.80 × 10⁻⁴ m². A tensile force of 720 N elongates it by 0.09 mm. What is Young’s modulus of this specimen?
C.explain:
EXTRACT — L = 0.15 m · A = 0.80 × 10⁻⁴ m² = 8.0 × 10⁻⁵ m² · F = 720 N · ΔL = 0.09 mm = 9.0 × 10⁻⁵ m
Step 1. Convert 0.09 mm before anything else. 0.09 mm = 0.09 × 10⁻³ m = 9.0 × 10⁻⁵ m.
Step 2. Y = (F × L) / (A × ΔL)
Numerator: 720 × 0.15 = 108
Denominator: (8.0 × 10⁻⁵) × (9.0 × 10⁻⁵) = 7.2 × 10⁻⁹
Y = 108 / 7.2 × 10⁻⁹ = 1.5 × 10¹⁰ Pa = 15 GPa
Trap 1.5 GPa is a missing power of ten. Trap 150 GPa used ΔL still in millimetres.

C.q: The shear deformation in the lecture is described as being 'somewhat like':
options: A pack of playing cards being pushed sideways
C.explain: The lecture compares shear deformation to a pack of playing cards — the top card slides horizontally relative to the bottom, with each intermediate card sliding a bit less.

C.q: Which of the following is the cleanest definition of a physical quantity?
options: Any number you can write down
Only things you can touch with your hands
A property that can be measured, expressed by a numerical value AND a unit, describing the state of a system
C.explain: A physical quantity requires BOTH a number and a unit.

C.q: Which of the following is a medical example of stress in the human body?
options: Blood pressure acting on vessel walls
C.explain: Blood pressure pushing on artery walls is stress — a force distributed over an area.

C.q: The SI prefix micro (µ) means which power of ten?
C.explain: Micro (µ) = 10⁻⁶. Nano (n) = 10⁻⁹. So 1 µm = 1000 nm.

C.q: Buoyant force 2352 N on a fully submerged box in fresh water (ρ=1000, g=9.8). Volume?

D.q: What is the density of a wooden block of dimensions 6 cm × 7 cm × 8 cm with mass 120 g?
Bulk modulus is calculated as:
D.explain: Bulk modulus = Hydraulic stress / Hydraulic strain = (F/A) / (ΔV/V). Units: Pa.

D.q: What is the net upward force on a submerged object if its weight is 250 N and the buoyant force is 320 N?
D.explain: Net = F_b − W = 320 − 250 = 70 N upward.

D.q: A blood vessel narrows from A₁ = 0.1 m² (V₁ = 0.5 m/s) to A₂ = 0.01 m². What is V₂?
D.explain: Using A₁V₁ = A₂V₂: V₂ = (A₁V₁) / A₂ = (0.1 × 0.5) / 0.01 = 5 m/s.

D.q: Pascal's principle states that:
options: Pressure in a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions
Buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced
D.explain: Pascal: an external pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally throughout.

D.q: What is the absolute pressure at a depth of 20 m in fresh water, given ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s², and P_atm = 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa?
Which of the following has BOTH a numerical value AND a unit, making it a complete physical quantity?
D.explain: 10 kg has both a number (10) and a unit (kg). The others are missing one part.

D.q: A diver is at a depth where the gauge pressure reads 4.41 × 10⁵ Pa in fresh water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²). How deep is the diver?
Young's modulus is calculated as:
D.explain: Young's modulus = Longitudinal stress / Longitudinal strain = (F/A) / (ΔL/L). Units: Pa.

D.q: Mass flow rate is defined as:
options: The pressure divided by the area
The force exerted by a fluid on the tube wall
The amount of volume passing a point per unit time
The amount of mass passing a given point per unit time
D.explain: Mass flow rate is the amount of mass that passes a given point per unit time.

D.q: In the bone diagram, the side being compressed is under ______ stress, while the side being stretched is under ______ stress.
D.explain: When a long bone bends, one side is squeezed (compressive) and the opposite side is stretched (tensile). Both are forms of longitudinal stress.

D.q: Why is the Young's modulus clinically useful for assessing bone health?
options: It indicates bone stiffness and resistance to elastic deformation, predicting fracture risk
D.explain: The Young's modulus reflects bone stiffness. A lower value (from osteoporosis or osteogenesis imperfecta) means greater fracture risk under normal loads.

D.q: Volume of a metal ball with mass 18 g and density 8 g/cm³?
Which of the following is an example of a crystalline solid from the curriculum review?
D.explain: Crystalline solids have a regular lattice. Curriculum examples: Ag, Au, Pb, Sn. Rubber is amorphous.

D.q: Which of the following is a correct equivalent for 1 atm?
D.explain: 1 atm = 760 torr (mmHg) = 14.7 lb/in² ≈ 1.013×10⁵ Pa.

D.q: Tensile stress applied to a material causes it to:
D.explain: Tensile stress pulls the material along its axis, causing elongation (stretching).

D.q: Which ordering of DIFFUSION rate is correct?
options: Diffusion is equal in all three
D.explain: Diffusion is fastest in gases because their molecules move fastest and are furthest apart.

D.q: Which statement about solids is FALSE?
D.explain: Solids are NOT easily compressed — strong intermolecular forces lock particles in place.

D.q: What are the two types of fluid flow described in the lecture?
D.explain: The lecture names two types of fluid flow: streamline (also called laminar) and turbulent.

D.q: What happens to a material loaded beyond its elastic limit?
options: It returns to its original shape
It deforms permanently and eventually breaks
D.explain: Past the elastic limit, deformation becomes permanent. Further loading reaches the breaking point where the material fractures.

E.q: Which formula correctly represents the modulus of elasticity?
E.explain: Modulus = Stress / Strain. Units: pascal (Pa), because strain is dimensionless.

E.q: Which of the following is the correct final formula for mass flow rate?
E.explain: Mass flow rate = ρ A v, where ρ is density, A is cross-sectional area, and v is the velocity of the fluid.

E.q: How does osteoporosis affect the Young's modulus of bone?
options: It lowers it, making bone brittle and easily fractured
It raises it, making bone stiffer
E.explain: Osteoporosis reduces bone density and lowers the Young's modulus. The bone becomes brittle and fractures under loads a healthy bone would tolerate.

E.q: How many base quantities does the SI system have, and what is the SI unit of temperature?
E.explain: The SI system has 7 base quantities, and temperature's base unit is the kelvin.

E.q: Rank the intermolecular forces from strongest to weakest across the three common states:
E.explain: Solids hold their molecules most tightly, gases least tightly.

E.q: Which expression gives the pressure at a depth h below the surface of a liquid of density ρ?
E.explain: Gauge (hydrostatic) pressure: P = ρgh.

E.q: In a manometer, the gauge pressure of a gas in a container is given by:
E.explain: Manometer gauge pressure equals the hydrostatic column: P_gauge = ρgh.

E.q: What is the constant of proportionality between stress and strain called?
E.explain: Modulus of elasticity = Stress / Strain. It is a material property within the elastic limit.

E.q: In the Système International (SI), which is the base unit of mass?
E.explain: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg). A newton is force. Grams are used on the bench but are 10⁻³ kg.

E.q: A femur 0.38 m long has cross-sectional area 3.0 × 10⁻⁴ m² and Young’s modulus 17 × 10⁹ Pa. The bone must not exceed a compressive strain of 0.008. What is the maximum compressive force it may carry?
E.explain:
EXTRACT — L = 0.38 m (not needed for force) · A = 3.0 × 10⁻⁴ m² · Y = 17 × 10⁹ Pa · max strain = 0.008 · find F
Step 1. Stress = Y × Strain = (17 × 10⁹) × 0.008 = 1.36 × 10⁸ Pa
Step 2. F = Stress × A = (1.36 × 10⁸) × (3.0 × 10⁻⁴) = 4.08 × 10⁴ N = 40 800 N
L was a decoy. Strain was already given, so you never compute ΔL. Trap 1.36 × 10⁸ N is the stress mistaken for a force.

E.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of pressure?
E.explain: Pascal (Pa) = N/m² is the SI unit of pressure.

E.q: A patient has a diastolic arterial pressure of 80 mm Hg. Approximately in kPa? (1 mmHg ≈ 133.3 Pa)
What is the buoyant force on a sphere of volume 0.6 m³ fully submerged in a fluid of density 850 kg/m³? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Loss of elasticity in blood vessels is significant because it:
E.explain: Arterial walls need elasticity to buffer the pulse and maintain diastolic pressure. Loss of elasticity contributes directly to cardiovascular disease.

E.q: Hydraulic stress produces which kind of deformation?
E.explain: Uniform pressure from all sides shrinks volume but preserves shape. The sphere in diagram (c) stays spherical.

E.q: Which one of the following three cubes of equal dimensions has the highest density?
E.explain: Same volume → highest mass means highest density. Gold ≫ wood or paper.

E.q: According to the lecture, normal blood flow in a healthy artery is:
options: A mix of laminar and turbulent
E.explain: Normal blood flow in a healthy artery is laminar — smooth and orderly.

E.q: Which statement about ideal liquids is correct according to the lecture?
options: Ideal liquids have stronger intermolecular forces than solids
Ideal liquids exist only as pure water
Ideal liquids are NOT compressible, but no ideal liquid exists in nature
E.explain: Ideal liquids are theoretically incompressible, but no real liquid achieves this.

E.q: A block measures 5.0 cm × 6.0 cm × 8.0 cm and has a mass of 960 g. What is its density?
Along a horizontal streamline (same height), Bernoulli says that if speed increases, pressure:
options: Becomes equal to atmospheric pressure only
E.explain: At constant h, P + ½ρv² = const → higher v means lower P.

F.q: Which pairing of stress and unit is correct?
F.explain: Stress = Force / Area, so its SI unit is N/m² = pascal (Pa).

F.q: Which statement best describes turbulent blood flow?
options: Smooth, orderly parallel layers with no mixing
Flow that only happens in the aorta
Flow that has no effect on energy or resistance
Irregular swirling movement that occurs when velocity becomes very high
F.explain: Turbulent flow is irregular swirling movement. It occurs when velocity becomes very high, and it increases energy loss and resistance.

F.q: Strain is best described as:
options: Deformation relative to original length; dimensionless with no units
Force per unit area; units are N/m²
F.explain: Strain = ΔL / L₀. It is a ratio, so it has no units.

F.q: Longitudinal strain is calculated as:
F.explain: Longitudinal strain = ΔL / L, where ΔL is the change in length and L is the original length. It is dimensionless.

F.q: Which is the MOST convenient reason mercury is used in barometers instead of water?
options: Mercury's high density gives a manageable column height
F.explain: High ρ_Hg → ~76 cm column vs ~10.3 m for water.

F.q: Which of the following is the correct form of Bernoulli's equation?
options: P₁ + ½ ρ v₁² + ρ g y₁ = P₂ + ½ ρ v₂² + ρ g y₂
P₁ × ½ ρ v₁² × ρ g y₁ = P₂ × ½ ρ v₂² × ρ g y₂
F.explain: Bernoulli's equation: P₁ + ½ ρ v₁² + ρ g y₁ = P₂ + ½ ρ v₂² + ρ g y₂, or compactly P + ½ ρ v² + ρ g h = Constant.

F.q: Shear modulus is calculated as:
F.explain: Shear modulus = Shear stress / Shear strain = (F/A) / (Δx/L). Units: Pa.

F.q: How much mass of fluid does a box of volume 0.4 m³ displace when fully submerged in fresh water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³)?
For an incompressible fluid, the equation of continuity simplifies to:
F.explain: When density is constant (typical for liquids), the ρ terms cancel: A₁ v₁ = A₂ v₂.

F.q: Hooke's Law states that stress and strain are proportional up to which point?
options: The proportional limit (also called the elastic limit)
F.explain: Up to the elastic limit, stress/strain = constant (Young's modulus). Beyond it, permanent deformation occurs.

F.q: How do you convert a density given in g/cm³ to kg/m³?
F.explain: 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³. Multiply g/cm³ by 1000 to get kg/m³.

F.q: At sea level, what is the value of standard atmospheric pressure in pascals?
What are the units of strain?
F.explain: Strain = ΔL/L — a length divided by a length, so the units cancel. Strain has no units.

F.q: Amorphous solids are characterised by:
options: No long-range orderly structure; they soften over a temperature range
A regular repeating atomic lattice and a sharp melting point
Being unable to deform under any load
F.explain: Amorphous = no long-range order; softens over a range. Rubber (and glass/polymers) are typical.

F.q: In the CGS system, the units of length, mass, and time are:
F.explain: CGS = centimetre – gram – second. FPS = foot – pound – second. MKS = metre – kilogram – second.

F.q: The pressure in a room is 1.368 × 10⁵ Pa. What force acts on a floor 5 m × 5 m?
Archimedes' Principle states that the magnitude of the buoyant force is equal to:
options: The weight of the fluid displaced by the object
The density of the object times volume
The weight of the submerged object
The mass of the object times g
F.explain: F_b = weight of fluid displaced = ρ_fluid V_displaced g.

F.q: What happens when a material is loaded beyond its elastic limit?
options: It returns to its original shape
F.explain: Beyond the elastic limit, deformation becomes permanent. Continue loading and the material reaches its breaking point.

F.q: Mass of a wooden block 6 cm × 8 cm × 4 cm with density 0.35 g/cm³?
Which of the following is a DERIVED quantity, not a base quantity?
F.explain: Area = length × length, so it is built from base quantities and is derived.

G.q: An open-tube manometer is used primarily to measure:
G.explain: Open-tube manometers measure gas pressure in a container via the liquid column difference.

G.q: What is the SI unit of pressure (P)?
G.explain: SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa) = N/m².

G.q: Which pair correctly distinguishes elasticity from plasticity?
options: Elasticity → returns to original shape after force removed; Plasticity → permanent deformation
Elasticity → permanent deformation; Plasticity → returns to original shape
G.explain: Elasticity = reversible deformation. Plasticity = permanent deformation.

G.q: What is the purpose of the mercury barometer developed by Torricelli?
G.explain: Torricelli's mercury barometer measures atmospheric pressure (~76 cm Hg column at 1 atm).

G.q: A bone under 5 × 10⁶ Pa of stress shows a strain of 0.0025. What is the Young's modulus of this sample?
G.explain: Y = stress / strain = (5×10⁶) / (2.5×10⁻³) = 2 × 10⁹ Pa = 2 GPa.

G.q: Air pressure 1.368×10⁵ Pa exerts force 3.42×10⁵ N on a table. Area of the table?
G.explain: A = F/P = 2.5 m².

G.q: A lumbar vertebral body is 25 mm high. Treat its effective Young’s modulus as 10 × 10⁹ Pa. The maximum compressive stress before collapse is 20 × 10⁶ Pa. How much can the vertebral height shorten?
G.explain:
EXTRACT — L = 25 mm = 0.025 m · Y = 10 × 10⁹ Pa · max stress = 20 × 10⁶ Pa · find ΔL
Step 1. Convert height first. 25 mm = 0.025 m.
Step 2. Strain = Stress / Y = (20 × 10⁶) / (10 × 10⁹) = 0.002
Step 3. ΔL = 0.002 × 0.025 = 5.0 × 10⁻⁵ m = 0.050 mm
Cancellous-style bone + short L → tiny shortening. Trap 5.0 mm used L still in millimetres inside Strain × L without converting.

G.q: Stress is defined as:
G.explain: Stress = F / A. SI unit: N/m² = Pascal (Pa).

G.q: Which of the following is NOT matter?
G.explain: Matter must have mass and occupy space. Light has neither rest mass nor volume — it is not matter.

G.q: Pressure gauge reads 1.39×10⁵ Pa (gauge) in fresh water (ρ=1000, g=9.8). Diver depth?
Femur: L = 0.4 m, Young's modulus = 16×10⁹ Pa, max stress = 150×10⁶ Pa. Find maximum compression ΔL before breaking.
G.explain: Strain = stress / Young's modulus = 150×10⁶ / 16×10⁹ = 0.009375. ΔL = strain × L = 0.009375 × 0.4 = 0.00375 m = 3.75 mm.

G.q: A tibia 0.35 m long has Young’s modulus 18 × 10⁹ Pa. It can withstand a maximum compressive stress of 140 × 10⁶ Pa before fracture. How much can this tibia compress before it breaks?
G.explain:
EXTRACT from the story — L = 0.35 m · Y = 18 × 10⁹ Pa · max stress = 140 × 10⁶ Pa · find ΔL
Step 1. Definition: Y = Stress / Strain, so Strain = Stress / Y
Strain = (140 × 10⁶) / (18 × 10⁹) = 0.140 / 18 = 0.007778 (no units)
Step 2. Strain = ΔL / L, so ΔL = Strain × L
ΔL = 0.007778 × 0.35 = 0.002722 m = 2.72 mm
Trap option 7.78 mm is the strain written as if it were millimetres. Trap 27.2 mm forgot to convert metres.

G.q: What is the velocity profile of laminar blood flow described as?
G.explain: Laminar blood flow has a parabolic velocity profile — highest in the centre, lowest near the wall.

G.q: Strain (ε) as used in these lectures is:
G.explain: ε = ΔL/L₀. Strain is dimensionless. Stress σ = F/A has units of Pa.

G.q: Volume flow rate is calculated as:
G.explain: Volume flow rate Q = A v, where A is cross-sectional area and v is velocity.

G.q: In a narrowed artery, Bernoulli's principle predicts:
G.explain: In a narrowed artery, velocity increases and pressure decreases. Blood supply to tissues may be reduced.

G.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five mechanical properties listed in the lecture?
G.explain: The five mechanical properties are elasticity, plasticity, ductility, malleability, and strength. Conductivity is an electrical/thermal property.

G.q: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of 25 m in a lake (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²)?
Which state of matter is described as having a definite size and shape and being unable to be compressed?
G.explain: Solids have definite shape and volume, high density, strong intermolecular forces, and cannot be compressed.

G.q: Hydraulic press: large piston 0.20 m², small 0.02 m². Force on small piston to lift 3000 N?

H.q: Which is the correct formula for stress?
H.explain: Stress = Force / Area. Units: N/m² = Pa.

H.q: Which set correctly pairs crystalline vs amorphous examples?
options: Crystalline: Ag, Au, Pb, Sn · Amorphous: rubber
Both rubber and gold are crystalline
H.explain: Crystalline: Ag, Au, Pb, Sn. Amorphous: rubber (also glass, many polymers).

H.q: According to Bernoulli's principle, as velocity increases:
H.explain: As velocity increases, pressure decreases. In symbols: v ↑ ⇒ P ↓.

H.q: Which statement best describes laminar blood flow?
options: Irregular swirling movement with mixing layers
Flow that always produces a murmur
Smooth and orderly movement; blood moves in parallel layers
Flow that only happens in veins
H.explain: Laminar blood flow is smooth and orderly. Blood moves in parallel layers. It is the normal flow in healthy arteries.

H.q: Kinetic energy of particles is temperature-dependent. Which statement is correct?
options: Kinetic energy does not depend on temperature
All three states have equal kinetic energy at the same temperature
Gases have the highest kinetic energy, solids the lowest
Solids have the highest kinetic energy
H.explain: Gases have the highest kinetic energy, solids the lowest — at the same temperature.

H.q: The SI prefix micro (µ) means which power of ten?
H.explain: Micro (µ) = 10⁻⁶. Nano (n) = 10⁻⁹. Example: 1 µm = 10⁻⁶ m = 1000 nm.

H.q: Mass flow rate ṁ through a tube equals:
H.explain: ṁ = ρAv (kg/s). Volume flow Q = Av (m³/s).

H.q: Diagram (c) shows a sphere shrinking in volume under pressure from a fluid. This represents:
H.explain: Uniform pressure applied from all directions producing a volume change ΔV without shape change is hydraulic stress.

H.q: The SI prefix nano (n) means which power of ten?
H.explain: Nano (n) = 10⁻⁹. Micro (µ) = 10⁻⁶. So 1 µm = 1000 nm.

H.q: Which statement best explains why liquids and gases are both classified as fluids?
options: They flow from higher to lower pressures and continuously deform under shear stress
They both have the same density
They both contain only one type of molecule
H.explain: Fluids continuously deform under shear and can flow. Solids keep a fixed shape.

H.q: Pressure on teeth during chewing is an example of:
H.explain: Chewing applies force over the tooth's contact area — force per area = stress.

H.q: A glass block measures 8 cm × 5 cm × 3 cm and has a density of 2.5 g/cm³. What is its mass?
A wooden block floats in water with 40% of its volume submerged. Total volume 0.02 m³, ρ_water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s². Buoyant force?
Absolute pressure on a swimmer 30 m deep in fresh water (ρ=1000, P_atm=1.0123×10⁵ Pa, g=9.8)?
A mercury barometer shows a column of 76 cm. If water were used instead, approximately how tall would the column need to be?
H.explain: Water is ~13.6× less dense than Hg, so the column is ~13.6× taller ≈ 10.3 m.

H.q: The pressure on an object at depth h in a liquid, measured from atmospheric level, is called:
H.explain: Gauge pressure is the excess over atmosphere: P_gauge = ρgh. Absolute = atm + gauge.

H.q: Which equation correctly relates absolute pressure, atmospheric pressure, and gauge pressure?
H.explain: P_abs = P_atm + P_gauge.

H.q: A patellar tendon is 0.12 m long and has Young’s modulus 1.2 × 10⁹ Pa. The maximum tensile stress it can carry before failing is 60 × 10⁶ Pa. What is the maximum elongation?
H.explain:
EXTRACT — L = 0.12 m · Y = 1.2 × 10⁹ Pa · max tensile stress = 60 × 10⁶ Pa · find ΔL
Step 1. Strain = Stress / Y = (60 × 10⁶) / (1.2 × 10⁹) = 60 / 1200 = 0.05
Step 2. ΔL = Strain × L = 0.05 × 0.12 = 0.006 m = 6.0 mm
This is tensile (قوة الشد), not compression — same two-step algebra as the femur. Tendon Y is much smaller than bone Y, so strain is larger.

H.q: A bone under stress 5×10⁶ Pa shows strain 0.0025. Young's modulus?
H.explain: Y = stress/strain = 5×10⁶/0.0025 = 2.0×10⁹ Pa.

H.q: Larger the Young's modulus of a material means:
options: Less stress is required to produce a small deformation
More stress is required to produce a small change in length
H.explain: Higher Young's modulus = stiffer material. More stress is required for the same strain.
